subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell CI smoke lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with only commands that already pass under Windows `pwsh`?
rationale: The requested coverage fits the test-infrastructure roadmap, but the active candidate changes recurring Windows runner scope and one selected command is failing in live CI.

options.title: Prove full command set
options.body: Keep `check:docs` and `build:strict-smoke` in scope, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes with redacted proof.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage for only already-passing contributor commands and track `build:strict-smoke` separately.

options.title: Defer CI cost
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing a recurring Windows smoke lane until runner budget and command ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Prove full command set
recommendation.body: Keep `check:docs` and `build:strict-smoke` in scope, but land only after the Windows `pwsh` lane passes with redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across the current Windows CI matrix and the adjacent PowerShell-safe docs tooling repair.
